newsitem.title: USA: Equity Inns sees FFO below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Equity Inns sees FFO below estimates.

text.p: Equity Inns Inc said on Tuesday that funds from operations (FFO) for the year could fall as much as $0.11 a share short of analysts' consensus estimate of $1.33 per share for 1996.

"By far, the lion's share of the shortfall can be attributed to unexpected delays in completing certain previously announced acquisitions," Phillip McNeill Sr., the chief executive officer, said in a statement.
In August, the company announced plans to buy seven hotels valued at about $50 million. All of them were expected to close in the third quarter.
Instead, the company completed the purchase of only four hotels valued at $28 million in the third quarter.
The closings on three hotels, valued at $23 million, were delayed because of certain seller-related issues, Equity said. Two of those deals were completed in the past week.
"Although these delays will impact both the third and fourth quarters, this is really a deferral rather than a reduction of FFO," said Howard Silver, Equity Inns' chief financial officer.
He said the delay would not affect the current dividend.
